newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB to announce new leadership within few days.
newsitem.headline: DKB to announce new leadership within few days.

text.p: Scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd will announce its new leadership plans within the next few days, company sources said.
The bank has already cancelled one management reshuffle plan amid public outrage following Thursday's arrests of four current and former DKB executives in connection with the loan scandal.

On May 23, DKB announced that its president Katsuhiko Kondo and chairman Tadashi Okuda were stepping down to take the blame for the bank's loans to Ryuichi Koike, the corporate racketeer at the heart of the scandal.

They were to be replaced by vice-president Ichiro Fujita as president and another vice-president Yoshiharu Mani as chairman, but the bank confirmed on Sunday that those appointments had been cancelled amid the public outrage.
Fujita, whose admitted knowledge of the loans was defended by DKB when his promotion was announced, had been scheduled to take over on June 27.

Four present and former DKB executives have been arrested on suspicion of giving 11.78 billion yen in uncollateralised loans, via a DKB affiliate, to Kojin Building Co., a realtor run by Koike's younger brother, between July 1994 and September 1996 in violation of the Commercial Code.
Both Koike and the younger brother were arrested in May on suspicion of violating the Commercial Code by taking some 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
DKB said on Sunday it was considering closing its general affairs department, the section which dealt with the racketeer, as part of its reform efforts.
"We are currently considering preventive measures (so similar incidents do not occur again), including closing down our general affairs department," said a company source.
Another company source said the bank has not yet decided whether Fujita would also resign as a director.
